Hi Alicia — great talking earlier. Per our discussion, here is a short recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap / current behavior:
- Active data: We perform logical deletion of customer records from primary stores and indexes. For hosted API customers, removal from active databases typically completes within 24–72 hours after requests are validated.
- Backups: Automated snapshots are retained per our backup policy (default 30 days for rolling snapshots; archived retention up to 90 days depending on plan). Backups are immutable by default and require a scheduled retention expiry.
- Logs: Access logs and operational logs are retained for 90 days by default. We can redact PII fields in logs earlier upon request, but full audit records (non-PII metadata) are maintained for security investigations.
- Proof of deletion: We can produce a deletion certificate and a simple audit trail showing the request, validation, and actions taken. For records removed from immutable backups, we provide the retention window and the earliest purge date unless the customer is on a Private deployment where we can run on-demand removal.

Attachments I’m attaching: RTBF_Checklist.pdf (walkthrough of our standard deletion workflow) and a draft DPA for your legal team to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Camila to coordinate with your legal/compliance to review the DPA and the RTBF checklist.
2) Please confirm whether you require expedited backup purging or a certificate for every deletion event. If you require on-demand purges from backups we should discuss deployment mode (Dedicated/Private) since hosted customers have limitations.
3) Quick follow-up call this week to align on timelines and any contract amendments.

Happy to jump on another call — I’m available tomorrow afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Alicia — quick answers to your questions below and suggested operational approach: 

1) Backups: Archived backups are immutable in the standard hosted configuration. We do not typically delete individual customer data from historical immutable backups on demand for hosted tenants because of operational and integrity constraints. However, for Dedicated or Private deployments we have an on-demand purge process (forensic deletion) we can run — it requires coordination with SRE and legal, and may incur an operational fee. For hosted customers, we can: 
   - Shorten snapshot retention windows going forward (policy change)
   - Offer an expedited retention reduction on a best-effort basis after contract amendment

2) Proof / certificate: We can provide a signed deletion certificate that includes the request id, timestamp, scope (resource ids), and the action taken. For deletions that occur only from active stores (within 24–72 hours) the certificate will be definitive. For data that may still exist in immutable backups we will provide the backup retention details and the earliest purge date.

3) Logs and redaction: We maintain structured access and operational logs. PII fields that may appear in logs (e.g., full email addresses, raw request payloads containing sensitive fields) are redacted via automated scrubbing prior to long-term storage. Redaction rules are part of our security policy and we can share a redaction field map under NDA if needed.

Operational proposal:
- If FinTechCo requires hard-delete from all stored artifacts within a shorter SLA, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.
- While legal reviews the DPA, we can provision a short-term exception: issue deletion certificates for active-store deletions and provide backup retention reports.

I attached a simple RTBF_Timeline_Table.xlsx that maps request -> active deletion -> backup expiry windows. Also adding a DocuSign link for the DPA so your legal can sign/route.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 AM PT to align on contract path and timeline.
